# Workstation's topology bar is authored by its controller, not the view

## Context

#18460's Contract Ledger row 1 (*View interaction*) requires "declarative wiring; no view-to-controller forwarding network". Measuring that row's population found **five** dispatch sites in `apps/workstation/view/`, and exactly one of them inverts *both* directions at once. That one is this leaf; the other four are a different shape and are enumerated below rather than folded in.

#18460 is labelled `enhancement`, so by `ticket-create-workflow §4` it must be one-PR-resolvable — its five ACs span view interaction, product policy, native effects and a physical line ceiling, which it is not. #18533 (row: park/re-show) was routed under #18304 rather than under #18460 because it was engine work. This leaf is the app-side counterpart, filed so a PR can carry a truthful `Resolves` instead of closing four unmet ACs.

## The Problem

`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` builds its own child by calling into its controller:

```javascript
me.add([{module: TourToolbar}, me.createStatusBar(), me.getController().createTopologyBar(), { ... }]);
```

`WorkspaceController#createTopologyBar()` returns a toolbar config. Two directions are wrong in one expression: a controller authoring view structure, and a view reaching into its controller for a child it owns. The four remaining sites are single-direction reach-through (`Viewport.mjs:59`, `:70`, `:151` addressing *another* component's controller; `Workspace.mjs:795` a `saveTopology` facade the Neural Link and `Viewport.mjs:153` both call as a shipped surface) — none of them has a controller producing view config, and removing the facade would break `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs:229`. They are the larger, riskier half and are explicitly out of scope here.

There is a second consequence, which is the reason this is not cosmetic. Because the bar is built once as a config literal, its per-participant recovery buttons are frozen at construction. `getPopupStates()` grows when a pane tears out (`Workspace.mjs:2140`) and shrinks when a popup host retires (`PopupWorkspace.mjs:154`), and the bar cannot follow either.

## The Architectural Reality

- A view controller is declared through the component's `controller` config and reaches *into* the view: `src/controller/Component.mjs:117` `getReference()` resolves via `component.down({reference})`, needing no mount.
- `src/controller/Component.mjs:44` binds `onComponentConstructed()` to the host's `constructed` event, which `src/core/Base.mjs:820` fires after `isConstructed` is set — i.e. after the view's own `construct()` has added its children. Its docblock names exactly this use: *"in case you need references"*. Eight in-repo controllers already override it, including the sibling `apps/workstation/view/TourController.mjs:50`.
- Declarative handler names resolve through the configured controller chain: `src/util/Function.mjs:158` `resolveCallback` sends a string handler to `scope.getController?.()?.getHandlerScope(fn, null)`. Nothing needs to close over the controller instance.
- `apps/portal/view/home/FooterContainer.mjs:26` (configured controller) with `:40` (referenced child) is the executed precedent #18460 cites.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/WorkspaceSet.mjs` exposes `ids()` and no change signal, so a live-membership refresh has no event to hang on today. That is an engine seam, and #18460's Out of Scope forbids building it here.

## The Fix

- The view declares the toolbar inline: `reference: 'topology-toolbar'`, the two authored buttons with declarative handler names, and the Group's undo/redo `actions` with their `bind` formatters reading `me.topologyGroupId` directly.
- `WorkspaceController#createTopologyBar()` is replaced by `syncTopologyBar()`, which reaches the bar through `getReference()` and replaces only the derived tail after `static authoredTopologyButtonCount`, so a resync cannot destroy what the view authored.
- Two declarative handlers (`onOpenTopologyWorkspace`, `onMountTopologyWorkspace`) read the addressed participant off `data.component.workspaceKey`.
- `onComponentConstructed()` performs the single population, giving behaviour parity with the config literal.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Surface | Authority | Required outcome | Refusal/recovery | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The topology bar's structure | The view, through its own `items`/`actions` config | Declared in `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`; no controller method returns view config | Ordinary component disposal | A prototype-call witness reading `reference`, the authored handler names, and the item count |
| Its per-participant tail | `WorkspaceController#syncTopologyBar` via `src/controller/Component.mjs:117` | Only items after `authoredTopologyButtonCount` are replaced | Returns `false` on an unreachable or destroyed bar; never assumes it synced | A real `toolbar.Base` under the controller: populate, resync to empty, then destroy |
| Population timing | `src/controller/Component.mjs:44` → `src/core/Base.mjs:820` | One population, at `onComponentConstructed` | None; parity with the current single build | The same witness asserts the bar is already filled before any explicit call |
| Handler routing | `src/util/Function.mjs:158` | String names only; no captured controller | Unresolved name is inert, as for any Neo handler | The declared names asserted against the controller's methods |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` declares the topology bar; `grep -n 'getController()' apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` returns no site that consumes view config from the controller. The PR reports the full before/after dispatch-site population, not just the one removed.
- [ ] The controller fills the bar through `getReference()` and cannot destroy the view-authored head. A witness populates, resyncs after the participant set empties, and asserts the authored two survive.
- [ ] The lifecycle wiring itself is witnessed, not just the method it calls: an arm that would go red if `onComponentConstructed()` stopped calling `syncTopologyBar()`.
- [ ] Behaviour parity is claimed and measured — the bar is populated exactly once, as today. The stale-after-tear-out limitation is reported as unchanged, with the missing `WorkspaceSet` signal named, and is not silently fixed here.
- [ ] Workstation's 43 unit witnesses and the full unit tier stay green at current head; the one stale caller (`test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/WorkspaceController.spec.mjs:128`) moves to the surface that now owns it, and the PR says which arms moved and why.
- [ ] Mutation controls: renaming the view's `reference`, removing the lifecycle call, and replacing the whole item list instead of its tail each redden a named arm, and each arm is named in the PR.

## Out of Scope

The four remaining view-to-controller dispatch sites (`Viewport.mjs:59` · `:70` · `:151` and the `Workspace.mjs` `saveTopology` facade) — cross-component reach-through and a shipped Neural Link surface, both larger shapes with their own callers. A membership-change signal on `WorkspaceSet`. Any change to what the bar's buttons do, to Group/history semantics, or to #18460's other Ledger rows.

## Avoided Traps

No ritual `getReference()` added to legitimize a role: the controller genuinely needs the child it did not declare. No new forwarding facade — one controller method is removed and one is added, both with real work. No refresh path wired to a signal that does not exist, which would be a new engine seam wearing an app-code disguise.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — no engine host, Group, projection or native-window contract is touched.
